note: WRITTEN, 140 items x 5 = 700 rows, four section_ids. (1) Code derivation (data/hyatt_2023_aggression.py): the table pools five administrations. prelim1_aeN[_r], prelim2_aeN and s1_aeN are the .sav column names AEN[_R] lower-cased with a study prefix; aeqNN is a number-preserving rename of Study 2's AE_N and Study 3's AEQN, pooled under one code. The OSF .sav files for prelim1/prelim2/Study 1/Study 2 carry NO variable or value labels (checked at both levels); only Study 3's .sav labels AEQ1-AEQ16. So text is tied to code by 'doc item number N == column AEN' using the authors' own per-version instrument docs (paper_order); Study 3's labels are data_labels and match the appendix doc 16/16 verbatim. Doc->study identification by item counts and sample sizes: Study-1 doc 84 items/prelim1 N=335; Study-2 doc 40 items/prelim2 (27 columns deposited, 323 rows); Study-3 doc 31 items/Study 1 31 columns N=308; Study-4 doc 16 items/Study 2 N=359. Live data equal the .sav files exactly (124 prelim/s1 items: max |mean diff| 0, n identical; aeq pooled means identical). prelim1 retains 66 of 84 items and prelim2 27 of 40 in the deposited files (the paper culls redundant/restricted-range items); not a defect of this table. (2) Verification (verify_hyatt_2023_aggression_aeq.R, VERDICT: PASS; status PARTIAL): paper Table 2 (Study 1 EFA) reproduced from s1 columns chosen by doc number, max |diff| .014 over 16 items (substituting s1_ae29 for s1_ae21 gives .063); Table 3 CFA lambdas reproduced for Study 2 and Study 3 at every position to <=.005; linked same-wording item means across the four MTurk samples r=.944/.976/.946 (p1->p2 24 pairs, p2->s1 21, s1->s2 16; permutation 99th pct <=.58); valence class 64/66, 27/27, 30/31. (3) SOURCE CONFLICT, resolved against the paper: Table 3 of the paper (and Table 2) prints the Harm to Self / Harm to Victim rows as vulnerable, hurt, watch back, trouble / really suffer, seriously hurt, quality of life, reputation. Those are Study 1's s1 column order (Table 2 is correct for Study 1). The appendix, the Study-2 instrument doc and Study 3's .sav labels all give aeq09-aeq16 = trouble, vulnerable, hurt, watch back / cause the other person pain, seriously hurt, reputation, quality of life. Table 3's loadings match the columns in order, so its row TEXT was carried over from Table 2. Data side: correlation structure of Study 2 and Study 3 against Study 1's same-text items fits the label order r=.943/.929 vs Table-3 order .894/.860. Shipped: label/appendix order. (4) Reverse scoring: prelim1_ae17_r, _ae19_r, _ae45_r, _ae47_r, _ae48_r are the doc's *R items and are stored reversed (17_r/19_r sit with positive items +.40/+.48, 47_r/48_r with negative -.49/-.26; prelim2_ae29 raw 4.06 vs 6 - prelim1_ae19_r 3.85), so their option_text is reversed (resp 1 = 'Very likely ...'), as done for burkert_2019_whoqol_bref. prelim2_ae29 and s1_ae19 (same wording) are stored raw (valence -.67/-.62) and ship the normal anchors. (5) Deviations from literal: trailing '*R' scoring markers and the '(item # from previous study)' parentheticals stripped from item_text; source typo 'the right thing do.' kept verbatim (it is in all docs and the Study 3 labels; the paper prints 'to do'). The Study-2 and Study-3 version docs (prelim2, s1 sections) print '2 = Somewhat likely' - a duplicate of 4; shipped as 'Somewhat unlikely' because the paper states the Study 1 labels were '2 = Somewhat Unlikely' 'as in the preliminary studies'. Anchors otherwise per doc: prelim1 'Neither likely nor unlikely', others 'Neither likely or unlikely'; the 1 and 5 labels carry the docs' '(i.e., ...)' glosses. Study 3's .sav value label for AEQ6 reads 5='Very unlikely' (every other AEQ item 5='Very likely'); treated as a labelling slip, not shipped. (6) section_prompt differs by version: prelim/s1 docs 'a series of statements about possible consequences', final appendix 'statements that describe possible consequences'; the aeq section ships the appendix wording although Study 2's own doc (AEQ - Study 4.docx) reads 'statements about'. Paper: the running stem was repeated above each cluster of ~10 items; shipped once in section_prompt. instructions blank (no text identical across all four versions). (7) Rights: the AEQ is the authors' own instrument, printed in full as the paper's appendix and on OSF; no fee/permission/NC/ND/redistribution clause found in any OSF doc or the manuscript. OSF node carries no licence field (response data already in IRW). Register has no AEQ row; none written. (8) Step 3b: live items match the AEQ exactly (counts per study match the docs), not another instrument in the battery.

note: Clean pass with one disclosed anchor override. WORDS and MAPPING: the study's own SPSS file 'AEQ_Study 3.sav' (OSF fuz6h, Data + Syntax/Study 3 Data + Syntax, https://osf.io/download/9sm3b/, sha256 9c2d66b0c6ced8b2a103ce247c942501148a5ca52ccd2cf7e9045aa1a176eb02). Its variable labels carry the wording of all 36 ACME items (36/36 labelled, shipped verbatim, none truncated or padded; the label for ACME_2Dr reads 'once and a while' and is kept as written). Code derivation: data/hyatt_2023_aggression.py selects columns matching ^ACME_\d+[CDR]r?$ from the Study 3 file and lowercases them (_norm_item), so item IS the source column name (ACME_10Dr -> acme_10dr); exempt pattern, mapping_basis=data_labels. The processing script reads a CSV export of this .sav; every one of the 36 items x 5 levels = 180 per-level counts in the .sav equals the live table exactly (live 13,779 rows, 228 ids, wave 1/2 = the .sav's Study variable). ANCHOR OVERRIDE: the .sav's value labels give 1=Strongly disagree..5=Strongly agree for all 36 items, but the 22 items whose names end in lowercase 'r' (1Cr,2Dr,5Dr,6Dr,10Dr,11Dr,12Rr,13Rr,14Cr,17Rr,18Dr,19Dr,20Dr,21Dr,22Rr,24Rr,26Dr,27Dr,31Cr,32Rr,35Cr,36Dr -- exactly the negatively worded items) are stored ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED. Evidence: their means are 3.8-4.6 on 1-5, e.g. 'Sometimes I enjoy seeing people cry' (21Dr) has 73% at 5, 'When my friends are having a good time I often get angry' (10Dr) 67%, 'I enjoy seeing strangers get scared' (6Dr) 63%, 'I think it's fun to push people around' (2Dr) 51% -- impossible as 'Strongly agree' in a general sample; and all 36 corrected item-rest correlations are positive (0.22-0.62), with 273 of 308 r-vs-non-r inter-item correlations positive (range -0.11 to +0.55), which raw storage of reverse-worded items would make predominantly negative. So option_text for those 22 items is shipped reversed (1=Strongly agree .. 5=Strongly disagree), the baka2023_bpnsf/burkert_2019_whoqol_bref precedent; the 14 non-r items keep the file's labels. instructions blank: the deposit (the .sav and the Study 3 syntax file; the OSF root documents were not opened for ACME instructions) carries no ACME instructions. Single section_id. Administered in English (English-language labels, English-language study), so no language/_translated columns. Step 3b: 36 items, 12 each Cognitive Empathy (C), Affective Resonance (R), Affective Dissonance (D), 1-5 agreement -- matches Vachon & Lynam (2016) ACME, a criterion measure in Hyatt et al. (2023) Study 3. Rights: the ACME originator is Vachon & Lynam (2016), Assessment 23(2), doi 10.1177/1073191114567941. No clause reserving a right (fee, permission, NC, ND, no-redistribution) was locatable; the EMERGE (UCSD) measure page https://emerge.ucsd.edu/r_2gmaiwq8d1jwws1/ carries only a site footer 'Copyright 2023 - All Rights Reserved', a notice about that page, not a term on the instrument (PANAS precedent). Silence = permission; no register row written. The OSF node reports no node_license; the response table is already in IRW, and the wording's rights rest on the originator as above. irw-validate --profile upload: ok.
public_note: The 22 items whose codes end in 'r' (e.g. acme_2dr, acme_12rr, acme_31cr) are stored already reverse-scored, so for them resp 1 = Strongly agree and 5 = Strongly disagree, the opposite of the source file's value labels; the option_text shipped here follows the stored direction, and higher resp means more empathy on every item
